My family has farmed this land for generations. I know Quzhou well — the soil here is good loam, the North China Plain. My father grew wheat and corn, I grow wheat and corn, and that is what the land is good for. My wife and I manage about 8 mu together, though at my age I hire the village machinery cooperative to do the heavy work — planting and harvesting. My knees cannot take it anymore.

For winter wheat, I plant in October after the autumn rains soften the ground. I buy improved seeds from the township supply station — the 矮抗58 variety has been reliable for me. I apply compound fertilizer as a base before planting and add urea at jointing time. I water four times: once before planting to moisten the bed, once in winter before the ground freezes, once at jointing, and once when the grain is filling. I spray twice — once for weeds after emergence, once for powdery mildew and aphids in spring. The cooperative does rotary tillage after the maize harvest so the soil is loose for wheat.

For summer maize, I plant immediately after wheat harvest in June — there is no time to waste. Hybrid seeds are the only sensible choice; everyone uses them now and the yield is much better. Summer rain usually does the work, but I water once if August is dry. I spray herbicide right after planting before the seedlings emerge. No-tillage — the wheat roots hold the soil and the machine can seed directly into the stubble.

I do not experiment with new crops. Cotton prices are unpredictable and I do not know how to manage it at my age. Vegetables need too much daily labor. Wheat and maize feed my family and give me enough to sell at market.
